stories.title: Brotherhood, Healing & Fists: Inside The Morehouse Boxing Club Changing What It Means To Fight
stories.summary: What started as a six-person sparring session in a group chat grew into the Morehouse College Boxing Club, now competing nationally and producing champions. The club uses boxing to build discipline, brotherhood, and confidence among students, becoming a powerful outlet for young Black men.
stories.extended_summary: One night in September 2021, sophomore Jacobey Bell invited a few friends to an impromptu sparring session. By the next evening, 200 people packed the hall to watch. The club is now the first HBCU team at the U.S. Intercollegiate Boxing Association National Tournament, with two national champions and an award-winning documentary. It's less about throwing punches and more about what fighting means when it's grounded in healing and fellowship.

stories.extended_summary: A tiny robot flaps its wings in a giant tank at MIT, then takes flight through air fans. Inspired by puffins that swim and fly with the same wings, researcher Raphael Zufferey and his team created a half-pound, three-foot-wingspan drone that seamlessly transitions between air and water. No one had ever done it at this scale. Biologist Glenna Clifton calls it 'beautiful,' and the potential is huge: fly to a reef, dive down to sample water, then fly back with data about whales or pollution.

stories.extended_summary: Amy Massey emailed a harm reduction advocate in 2016, convinced she was dying. Heavy ketamine use had destroyed her bladder, and doctors said removal was the only option. Then she found Mat Southwell's YouTube video on reducing harm. Following his strategies, her symptoms improved so much that surgery was cancelled. Today, Massey works alongside Southwell as a peer trainer, teaching doctors and policymakers what works. 'When you go to a drug service, there's nothing on ketamine. They're asking us the questions,' she says.
